sections.title: General Risks and Possible Complications
paragraphs: I understand that wisdom tooth removal is a surgical procedure and that possible risks and complications include:

options.label: Damage to adjacent teeth, fillings, crowns or other dental work
Fracture of the tooth or root during removal
Retention of a small root fragment where removal would present a greater risk
Damage to surrounding gum, bone or soft tissues
Need for further treatment, review or referral if complications occur
Rare risk of jaw fracture, particularly in complex cases

sections.title: Lower Wisdom Teeth – Nerve Injury
paragraphs: I understand that the roots of lower wisdom teeth can be close to important nerves, particularly the inferior alveolar nerve (IAN) and lingual nerve.
Injury or irritation to these nerves can result in altered sensation, numbness, tingling, burning or other sensory changes affecting areas including the:
I understand that these changes may be temporary or, in some cases, prolonged or permanent.
Where relevant, my clinician has discussed the relationship between my wisdom tooth/teeth and the nerve as seen on my X-rays and/or CBCT scan.

sections.title: Coronectomy
paragraphs: Where a lower wisdom tooth is considered to be in close proximity to the inferior alveolar nerve, a coronectomy may be discussed as an alternative to complete removal.
I understand that a coronectomy involves removing the crown of the tooth while intentionally leaving the roots in place to reduce the risk of nerve injury.
I understand that retained roots may move, become exposed, become infected or require further treatment/removal at a later date.

sections.title: Upper Wisdom Teeth – Sinus Risks
paragraphs: I understand that upper wisdom teeth may be situated close to the maxillary sinus.
Removal can occasionally result in an opening between the mouth and sinus (oro-antral communication), which may require additional treatment or surgical repair.
There is also a small risk of a tooth or root fragment being displaced into the sinus or surrounding tissues, which may require further treatment or referral.

consentStatements: The proposed procedure and reason for treatment have been explained to me.
I have been given information about the expected benefits, material risks and reasonable alternatives relevant to me.
I have had the opportunity to ask questions and these have been answered to my satisfaction.
Relevant X-rays/CBCT findings have been discussed with me where appropriate.
I have informed the clinician of my current medical conditions, medications, allergies and any changes to my medical history.
I understand that no guarantee can be given regarding the outcome of treatment.
I understand that unexpected findings during surgery may require the treatment plan to be altered where clinically necessary and appropriate.
I understand that I may withdraw my consent at any time before the procedure.
I voluntarily consent to the wisdom tooth procedure described above.
clinicianDeclaration: I confirm that I have discussed the proposed procedure with the patient, including the reason for treatment, expected benefits, material and patient-specific risks, reasonable alternatives and the consequences of declining treatment.
Where appropriate, relevant imaging findings and the relationship of the tooth/teeth to the inferior alveolar nerve, lingual nerve and/or maxillary sinus have been discussed.
The patient has been given the opportunity to ask questions and has indicated that they understand the information provided.
